skill.name: api-mitmproxy
skill.description: Guides authorized API security testing with mitmproxy, including HTTPS traffic inspection, request modification, replay, scripting, mobile testing, and HAR export.
skill.summary: Use mitmproxy to inspect, modify, replay, and document authorized API traffic tests.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Static review confirmed a remote install script piped to bash and examples that bind mitmproxy to all interfaces. Semantic review confirmed dual-use TLS interception, pinning bypass, token capture, and business logic manipulation guidance. Most rule and reference template alerts are benign documentation examples.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to bash in the CI template.
remediation.suggestion: Use a pinned action, verified package manager install, or checksum-verified release artifact instead of curl to bash.

remediation.issue: Proxy and mitmweb examples bind to 0.0.0.0.
remediation.suggestion: Default examples to localhost and document authentication, firewall, and network scope controls for remote access.

remediation.issue: TLS interception and pinning bypass guidance can be misused outside authorized tests.
remediation.suggestion: Add stronger scope checks, written authorization reminders, lab-only defaults, and rollback steps near each workflow.

remediation.issue: Authentication token capture examples may expose sensitive values.
remediation.suggestion: Redact token output, avoid storing raw tokens, and add secure handling guidance next to the addon sample.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting suggests recursive deletion of the mitmproxy directory.
remediation.suggestion: Replace destructive cleanup with a backup or targeted certificate regeneration command and explain data loss impact.

semantic_findings.title: Dual-use TLS Interception and Pinning Bypass Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill guides certificate installation, reverse proxying, host redirection, and SSL pinning bypass for mobile API traffic. These steps are valid in authorized testing but can enable unauthorized HTTPS interception if misused.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines explicitly describe certificate trust setup, host redirection, and SSL unpinning tools for interception. The surrounding security caveats reduce malicious certainty but not dual-use risk.

semantic_findings.title: Authentication Token Capture Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The skill includes an addon pattern that stores authorization tokens and prints a token prefix during traffic analysis. Captured authentication material can expose accounts if logs or flow files are mishandled.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code sample explicitly collects authorization headers and prints part of each token. The skill also acknowledges captured traffic may contain credentials and PII.

semantic_findings.title: Business Logic Manipulation Examples
semantic_findings.description: The skill demonstrates changing request headers and WebSocket message content to test authorization and role behavior. This is useful for authorized assessment but can support privilege abuse against systems outside scope.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited examples modify user identity headers and replace WebSocket content from user to admin. They are presented for testing, so risk is dual-use rather than clearly malicious.

content.value_statement: API security testing needs clear visibility into live request and response behavior. This skill guides authorized mitmproxy workflows for inspection, modification, replay, and reporting.
actual_capabilities: Explains setup for mitmproxy, mitmweb, and mitmdump interfaces.
Guides interactive API inspection, request modification, replay, and HAR export.
Shows Python addon patterns for authentication testing, fuzzing, GraphQL, and WebSockets.
Documents certificate installation steps for browser, Android, and iOS testing.
Includes CI testing patterns and security scan templates for API workflows.
Adds security considerations for captured traffic, storage, access control, and authorization.
limitations: Requires mitmproxy tools and client proxy configuration.
Only applies to systems where the user has explicit testing authorization.
SSL pinning bypass depends on device, operating system, and application controls.
Does not replace full manual validation of security findings.

use_cases.title: Inspect API Requests
use_cases.description: Capture and review request headers, tokens, parameters, and responses during an authorized web API test.

use_cases.title: Debug Mobile API Traffic
use_cases.description: Configure a test device through mitmproxy and document mobile app API behavior in a controlled lab.

use_cases.title: Automate Regression Checks
use_cases.description: Use mitmdump scripts and saved flows to repeat focused API security checks in a CI workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Safe Capture
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a local web API test.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me set up mitmproxy for an authorized local API test. Include proxy setup, certificate steps, and safe storage guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Review Authentication Traffic
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate analysis of login and session behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through reviewing captured authentication traffic. Focus on token handling, replay risk, authorization checks, and redaction.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Mobile Test
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for a controlled mobile lab.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a mobile API testing plan using mitmproxy. Include scope controls, certificate setup, pinning constraints, and evidence handling.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Automation Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced CI or repeatable security testing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a mitmdump-based API security regression workflow. Include captured flow handling, addon goals, failure criteria, and data protection.

output_examples.input: I need to inspect an authorized staging API login flow.
output: A scoped capture plan with proxy setup, certificate installation, and test account boundaries.
A checklist for reviewing headers, cookies, tokens, status codes, and error messages.
A reporting outline that redacts credentials and stores flow files securely.

output_examples.input: I want to repeat API checks during CI without exposing secrets.
output: A mitmdump workflow outline that runs tests through a local proxy.
Guidance for redacting captured values before saving artifacts.
Failure criteria based on known authentication, authorization, and input validation checks.

output_examples.input: A mobile app uses certificate pinning in a lab build.
output: A controlled test plan that confirms authorization, lab devices, and rollback steps.
Options for proxy configuration and certificate trust review.
Notes on documenting pinning behavior without collecting unnecessary user data.

best_practices: Test only systems and traffic covered by written authorization.
Redact tokens, cookies, personal data, and secrets before saving or sharing captures.
Bind proxy services to localhost unless remote access is required and protected.
anti_patterns: Do not intercept production or third-party traffic without explicit approval.
Do not commit flow files, HAR files, certificates, or captured credentials to source control.
Do not expose mitmweb or proxy listeners on public networks without authentication and firewall controls.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps plan and run authorized mitmproxy workflows for API traffic inspection, modification, replay, and reporting.

faq.question: Can it test HTTPS APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains certificate installation and proxy setup needed to inspect HTTPS traffic in a controlled environment.

faq.question: Is this appropriate for production traffic?
faq.answer: Only with explicit authorization, strict scope, secure storage, and privacy controls. Lab and staging environments are safer defaults.

faq.question: Does it include automation guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers mitmdump scripts, saved flows, replay, HAR export, and CI-oriented test patterns.

faq.question: What tools must be installed?
faq.answer: The workflows require mitmproxy tools and Python support for addon scripts. Mobile tests may require device-specific setup.

faq.question: How should captured secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Treat captures as sensitive data. Redact credentials, restrict access, encrypt storage, and delete files when no longer needed.
